newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Bagel stock plunges after earnings report.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Bagel stock plunges after earnings report.

text.p: New York Bagel Enterprises Inc. stock lost a third of its value Monday after the company announced a fourth-quarter earnings projection that was lower than analysts had expected.

The stock fell $2.25 to $4.50 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq after New York Bagel said it expected earnings for the quarter of 4 cents to 5 cents a share, up from year-ago earnings of 2 cents a share.
"The analysts were looking for a stronger number. I think they were reading in the seven cent to eight cent range," Paul Hoover, vice president, strategic planning, said.
Sales rose to $3.3 million from $2 million, the company said.

The Chicago-based company said higher labour costs and higher depreciation and amortization expenses from new restaurant openings and the Lots A' Bagels acquisition, completed in December, tempered earnings growth in the quarter.
"I do look at them as short-term costs," Hoover said.
New York Bagel had 33 bagel restaurants at year-end, up from 15 at the end of 1995, with 10 units acquired or built in the fourth quarter alone, he said.
